entries.title: II Chronicles 32:3
segments: Stop the waters; this was done by carrying them into the city in an underground channel,

entries.title: II Chronicles 32:5
segments: Millo; a citadel or fortress in Jerusalem.

entries.title: II Chronicles 32:7
segments: Those who have God for their helper have more for them than can ever be against them.

entries.title: II Chronicles 32:8
segments: Rested themselves; believed what Hezekiah said, and depended upon its fulfilment.

entries.title: II Chronicles 32:9
segments: Lachish; in the south part of Judah.

entries.title: II Chronicles 32:10
segments: Implicit confidence in God often appears to worldly men foolish and absurd; and they expect no more from him, than they do from the idols of the heathen.

entries.title: II Chronicles 32:15
segments: How much less; as if Jehovah were less powerful than idols.

entries.title: II Chronicles 32:16
segments: Speaking against the Lord is a preparation for experiencing his wrath.

entries.title: II Chronicles 32:20
segments: Prayer to God in trouble is the never failing resource of his people.

entries.title: II Chronicles 32:25
segments: Even good men, if left to themselves when greatly blessed of God, instead of rendering to him gratitude and praise, will be lifted up with pride, and thus draw down upon themselves his chastisements.

entries.title: II Chronicles 32:29
segments: As all earthly substance comes from God, men should receive it as his gift, view it as his property, and use it according to his will.

entries.title: II Chronicles 32:30
segments: Gihon; a fountain on the west side of Jerusalem.  See note to

entries.title: II Chronicles 32:31
segments: God often leaves men to themselves to try them, that they and others may know what is in their hearts, and to lead them to trust in him. They will then be as mount Zion that cannot be moved, and in seeking him as their portion they will not want any good thing.
